Core concepts

Static files

Serve a directory with serveStatic, and send individual files with res.sendFile, res.download and res.attachment.

serveStatic(root, options)#

serveStatic() is middleware. It resolves each request path inside root and, when it finds a file, streams it with the correct headers. When it doesn't, it hands control to the next layer.

js
import { App, serveStatic } from 'routiva';

const app = new App();
app.use(serveStatic('public', { maxAge: '1h' }));

App.serveStatic() and the App.static alias point at the same function.

Options#

OptionDefaultBehaviour
fallthroughtrueMisses call next(); set false to answer missing files with 404
dotfiles'ignore''ignore' skips, 'deny' returns 403, 'allow' serves them
index['index.html']Files tried when the path resolves to a directory; false disables indexing
extensions[]Extensions appended when the exact path is not a file
redirecttrueRedirect directory requests instead of resolving them
maxAge0Sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=…; 0 emits no cache header
immutablefalseAppends immutable to Cache-Control when maxAge is set
etagtrueEmit a weak ETag; false disables it
headersunsetObject of extra headers set on every response
typeunsetOverrides the Content-Type derived from the file extension

redirect defaults to true, but the current findFile never produces a redirect target, so a directory with no matching index falls through (or 404s) rather than redirecting. A directory is only served through its index list.

What it handles#

  • Methods. Only GET and HEAD. Every other method calls next() immediately, so it composes with POST routes on the same path.
  • Traversal. The path is percent-decoded, normalised and joined to root, then verified to stay inside it. ..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd resolves outside the root and is rejected. A NUL byte is rejected too.
  • Dotfiles. Files or directories whose name starts with . follow the dotfiles policy. 'ignore' is the safe default.
  • Index files. A request for a directory walks the index list in order and serves the first match that is a regular file.
  • Extension fallback. If the exact path is neither a file nor a directory, each entry of extensions is tried in order.
  • Fallthrough. If nothing is found, next() runs unless fallthrough is false, in which case the middleware raises HttpError(404).

Path resolution#

resolveWithin(root, requestPath, dotfiles) returns an absolute path, null to skip, or 'deny':

Request pathResult
/style.css<root>/style.css
/..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswdnull (escapes root)
/a/%00bnull (NUL byte)
/.env with dotfiles: 'ignore'null
/.env with dotfiles: 'deny''deny' → 403
/.env with dotfiles: 'allow'<root>/.env

Index and extension examples#

js
// Serve public/index.html for "/", public/index.htm as a fallback.
app.use(serveStatic('public', { index: ['index.html', 'index.htm'] }));

// Disable directory indexes entirely.
app.use(serveStatic('public', { index: false }));

// GET /about serves public/about.html.
app.use(serveStatic('public', { extensions: ['html'] }));

Extension fallback runs only after the exact path and directory index checks fail, so it never shadows a real file.

Conditional and range requests#

File responses are handled by send.js, the same engine res.sendFile() uses. For every file it sets Last-Modified, Accept-Ranges: bytes and a weak ETag of the form W/"<size-hex>-<mtime-hex>".

text
stat file
   │
   ├─ If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since still fresh ─▶ 304 (no body)
   ├─ Range: bytes=a-b ─▶ 206 + Content-Range, stream the slice
   ├─ bad range ─▶ 416 + Content-Range: bytes */size
   └─ else ─▶ 200 + Content-Length, stream the file

Matching rules:

  • If-None-Match: * is always fresh. Otherwise the header is split on commas and each tag is compared for exact equality with the ETag. With etag: false the check is skipped.
  • If-Modified-Since is compared at whole-second resolution, because HTTP dates carry no milliseconds.
  • A range request must match bytes=<start>-<end> exactly. Multiple ranges in one header are not supported — an unrecognised value is treated as no range.

Valid forms:

HeaderMeaning
bytes=0-499First 500 bytes
bytes=500-From byte 500 to the end
bytes=-500Last 500 bytes
bytes=0-0A single byte

A suffix of 0, or a start beyond the file size, is answered with 416.

Caching#

maxAge is parsed by parseDuration, which accepts numbers or strings like '500ms', '30s', '10m', '1h', '7d'.

js
// Hashed assets: cache for a year, safe because the name changes on edit.
// Note the largest duration unit is weeks, so a year is expressed as 365d.
app.use('/assets', serveStatic('public/assets', { maxAge: '365d', immutable: true }));

// HTML: revalidate on every request.
app.use(serveStatic('public', { etag: true, maxAge: 0 }));

Only when maxAge is greater than zero is Cache-Control: public, max-age=… sent, with , immutable appended when requested. With the default maxAge: 0 no Cache-Control header is written, so clients fall back to the ETag and Last-Modified revalidation above.

res.sendFile() and res.download()#

Single-file responses reuse the same engine:

js
app.get('/report', (req, res) => {
  res.sendFile('reports/q3.pdf');            // inline
});

app.get('/report/download', (req, res) => {
  res.download('reports/q3.pdf', 'Q3 2026.pdf');
});
  • res.sendFile(filePath, options?, callback?) resolves the path against the process working directory and accepts the same maxAge, etag, headers and type options as serveStatic(). It returns a promise; if you pass a callback it returns this.
  • A missing file rejects with HttpError(404), so it flows into your error middleware.
  • res.download(filePath, filename?, options?, callback?) is sendFile plus a Content-Disposition: attachment header. Arguments shift: a function filename is treated as the callback, and an object filename is treated as options.
  • res.attachment(filename?) sets Content-Disposition: attachment on its own. Non-ASCII names get an RFC 5987 filename*=UTF-8''… parameter alongside a sanitised ASCII filename.

MIME types#

lookupMime(filePath) maps an extension to a type using a built-in table, and falls back to application/octet-stream. The table covers HTML, text, Markdown, JSON, JS, CSS, XML, CSV, YAML, the common image and font formats, audio, video, WASM, PDF, ZIP and gzip.

js
import { lookupMime } from 'routiva';

lookupMime('app.css');   // 'text/css; charset=utf-8'
lookupMime('photo.webp'); // 'image/webp'
lookupMime('archive.rar'); // 'application/octet-stream'

res.type(value) uses its own small extension table, so res.type('html') works as shorthand for text/html; charset=utf-8.

Single-page app fallback#

Mount the static handler first, then a catch-all route that returns the shell for any remaining GET. Anything the static layer didn't find lands here.

js
import { App, serveStatic } from 'routiva';

const app = new App();

app.use(serveStatic('dist', {
  index: ['index.html'],
  extensions: ['html'],
}));

// Client-side routes: /settings, /users/42, … all return the SPA shell.
app.get('*', (req, res) => {
  res.sendFile('dist/index.html');
});

app.listen(3000);

Because serveStatic() falls through by default, real assets like /app.abc123.js are streamed from disk and only the unknown paths reach the catch-all. If you serve the API from the same app, register those routes before the catch-all so they match first.
